fit: metabolic parkinsonism case with a diet and medication timeline
assessment: Suspected visual hallucinations improved after pramipexole withdrawal. Earlier phenylalanine restriction and later motor levodopa testing are distinct observations.

fit: Parkinson visual-cue experiment with older and younger controls
assessment: The Necker cube experiment measures dominance and switching of interpretations of a present image. Spontaneous hallucination frequency is a different endpoint.

fit: OPA1 family phenotype and clinical visual hallucination presence
assessment: A syndromic case reported visual hallucinations. Genetic and optic findings and clinical presence constrain inference to the documented phenotype.
A variant carrier developed visual hallucinations and later bradykinesia. The order of findings is useful for phenotype comparison and has no dietary comparison.

fit: preceding-month NPI in Lewy body and Alzheimer dementias
assessment: The Lewy body group scored higher on the NPI hallucinations domain. The composite and group comparison cannot supply a Parkinson visual episode rate.

fit: diagnostic imaging with hallucination presence by group
assessment: Baseline clinical feature counts contextualize the DAT SPECT and cardiac MIBG comparison. The report has no clinical food intervention.

Two of 450 participants converting from immediate-release carbidopa-levodopa discontinued for visual hallucinations. The count covers clinical withdrawals prior to randomization, not the randomized or overall event rate.

fit: visual symptom presence before conversion to Lewy body or Alzheimer dementia
assessment: Nine of 25 Lewy body converters and one Alzheimer converter had reported visual hallucinations at the mild cognitive impairment stage. Person counts do not establish episode frequency.

fit: antipsychotic trial synthesis using varied psychosis measures
assessment: Clozapine and pimavanserin results differ from inconclusive quetiapine and olanzapine trials. The review aggregates original evidence families and has no food comparison.

fit: historical synthesis of medicinal alkaloids and single-vine extract
assessment: This secondary viewpoint describes the single adverse event in the 2001 trial as visual, while the primary paper leaves modality unspecified. One attributed event cannot estimate dried fig effects.

fit: ATP13A2 juvenile parkinsonism case contrasted with earlier phenotypes
assessment: The reported patient had no hallucinations, although visual hallucinations are described in earlier cases. This concerns genetic parkinsonism and lacks a food exposure.

fit: randomized single-vine extract versus manzanilla in early Parkinson disease
assessment: The extract arm improved on the motor total with worse resting tremor. The original records one transient hallucination labeled without modality in the event table. This is a different plant and preparation.

fit: Dravet syndrome cohort and repeated AES member
assessment: Eleven of 12 adults had parkinsonian features and selected patients improved after levodopa. The same findings appear at AES 2014. No food or visual episode frequency was evaluated.

fit: pediatric PRES case with EEG and visual hallucinations
assessment: The observed visual episodes tracked seizure activity in the selected case. The clinical setting, age group and mechanism differ from the frozen exposure and population.

fit: epilepsy and non-epilepsy randomized-trial safety summary
assessment: Two placebo visual hallucination reports and two differently coded psychotic-disorder reports in active epilepsy trial arms are subject to selected coding and context. These data do not involve dried fig intake or Parkinson disease.
